Proclamation 1975,

A. PROCLAMATION to establish certain Village Courts and to specify
the areas of those courts,

MADE by the High Commissioner by virtue of the powers conferred by
Section 5 of the Village Courts Act 1973,
     as amended to date, and all other powers him enabling.

1. ESTABLISHMENT OF VILLAGE COURTS.
     The Village Courts specified in Column 1 of the Schedule are
hereby established.

2. VILLAGE COURT AREAS.
     The area of a Village Court specified in Column 1 of the
Schedule consists of the area—
        (a) deemed by customary usage to be occupied by the members
of the Village Groups set out in Column
            2; or
        (b) occupied by the persons residing on the prtions of land
set out in Column 2,
as the case may be.

PRICES ORDER No. 142
being
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for aviation
gasoline.

MADE by the Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to come
into operation on the date of publication in the Government Gazette.
1. DEFINITIONS.
In this Order—
"aviation gasoline" includes any substance normally sold as aviation
gasoline whether or not containing
additives of any kind;
"supplier" in relation to aviation gasoline, means a person or a
firm who sells aviation gasoline for the
purpose of consumption or use;
"retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
2. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE.
(i) Where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality specified in
Column I of Schedule I, the maximum price
per gallon at which the aviation gasoline may be supplied is the
maximum retail selling price specified in Column
2 of that Schedule in relation to the locality concerned; and
(ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of aviation gasoline,
supplied at any one time, calculated in
accordance with Subclause (1) is an amount involving a fraction of a
toea, the supplier may charge to the next
whole toea; and
(iii) Where aviation gasoline is supplied at a locality specified in
Column I of Schedule II, the maximum
surcharge for each aircraft specified in Column 2 of that Schedule
in relation to the locality concerned may be
charged by the supplier in addition to the maximum retail selling
price specified in Subclause (1).
3. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT.
Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
aviation gasoline to the Government, to Australia
or to a Statutory Authority of the Government or of Australia.

                    APPLICATIONS FOR STUDY PLACES 1974-75
   There are two forms of study assistance available in this Scheme,
both are administered by the Public Service
Board's Training Section. The awards are known as Lahara Study
Places. The awards are available at the Univer-
sity of Papua New Guinea. (Teachers should apply for the Lahara
Session through the Department of Education as
in previous years.)
                                DIVISION A
Division A—Pre-matriculation Course
   Places in this Division will be strictly limited. Officers who
are awarded a place are advised that successful
completion of the Lahara Pre-matriculation Course does not provide
them with an educational qualification
of any type. No certificate is issued on successful completion of
the course. The course is only intended to serve
as a means of assessing the student's suitability for taking up
degree studies at the University. Officers applying
for places in Division A should only be those whose matriculation
status is not sufficient to commence degree
studies. (See also notes below.)
Eligibility
   Any permanent officer of the National Public Service.
                                DIVISION B

Division B—Degree Unit Courses
   This Division is intended to assist permanent officers of the
National Public Service who, through their
location or the nature of their duties have been prevented from
undertaking part-time University studies.
Eligibility
     (a) Permanent officers in the Port Moresby area who have
already completed part of their degree on
        a part-time basis.
     (b) Permanent officers transferred to Port Moresby within less
than one University of Papua New Guinea
        semester of application.
     (c) Permanent officers who are certified by their Department to
be prevented from undertaking part-
        time studies through the nature of their duties.
     (d) Permanent officers outside Port Moresby.


July, 1975                    2             Papua New Guinea Gazette

                  PUBLIC SERVICE LAHARA SCHEME—continued

        CONDITIONS APPLICABLE TO BOTH DIVISION A AND DIVISION B
Selection Criteria

    (a) Applicants must be acceptable to the Lahara Studies
Committee of the University of Papua New Guinea.
    (b) Departmental recommendation.
    (c) Service record.

Benefits

    (a)    Study leave with full pay.
    (b)    Fares will be paid where applicable for the officer (not his
family)
    (c)    A book allowance.
    (d)    Tuition and other compulsory fees are paid.

Duration

   A Lahara Study Place will apply only to the Lahara Session for
which it was granted. This generally covers
a period of six to eight weeks from 24th November to 16th January
1976. The successful completion of Lahara
studies does not give automatic entitlement to further studies
assistance,

Enrolment in Course

   Applicants for Lahara Study Places must ensure that at the time
of applying for this award they also apply
to the University for admission to the course. Enrolment forms are
available from University of Papua New
Guinea, Box 4820, University Post Office.

Closing Date

   The 15th August, 1975. Application Forms are available from the
Department of the Public Service Board's
Training Section but must be forwarded through the applicant's
Departmental Head to the Public Service Board,
Training Section, P.O. Ward Strip. Late applications will not be
accepted.

                                               RETURNS OF INCOME
.1 JOHN WOLFGANG LOHDERGER, Acting Chief Collector of Taxes, by
virtue of the powers conferred by the
   Papua New Guinea Income Tax Act 1959, as amended and all other
powers me enabling, hereby require
returns of all income derived during the year ended on the thirtieth
day of June, 1975 (or the accounting period,
if any, adopted under that Act in lieu of that year), to be
furnished to me in such of the forms provided for
the purpose as are applicable, containing the information and
particulars mentioned or referred to in the relevant
forms, and verified by declarations as therein set forth, and
accompanied by all such balance sheets, profit and
loss accounts, statements and other documents as are mentioned in
the forms or as are requisite, at the appropriate
places, on or before the dates hereinafter stated.

A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for Aviation

     Made by the Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulations Act 1949, as amended to date,


to come into operation on the date of publication in the Government
Gazette.

1. REVOCATION.


     Prices Order No. 142 is hereby revoked.


2. DEFINITIONS.


     In this Order—


       "aviation gasoline" includes any substance normally sold as

                  MAXIMUM PRICES FOR MANUFACTURED CIGARETTES
  MILTON FREDERICK ROBERTS, a Deputy Price Controller, by virtue of
the powers conferred by the Prices
  Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, do hereby make the
following Order:—
                                PRICES ORDER No. 143
1. CITATION
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No, 143.
2. COMMENCEMENT
   This Order shall come into operation on the date of publication
of this Order in the Gazette.
3. REVOCATION
   Prices Order No. 124 is hereby revoked.
4. DEFINITIONS
   In this Order—
     "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua
New Guinea from imported or locally
        grown tobacco leaf.
     "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
5. MAXIMUM PRICE
   (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at any of the locations specified
in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and pack
specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
   (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at locations other than those
specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third Column
of Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
6. DISPLAY OF PRICES
   A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order
applies for sale by retail, or who offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display
a ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent
position in clear and legibe figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting suds cigarettes, the price at which the
cigarettes concerned may be bought.
7. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS
   Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a notice in writing
is given by the Controller to a supplier of
cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not
less than fixed by Clause 5 of this Order, the maximum price at
which cigarettes may be so supplied is the price
fixed in that Notice.
